Confirmed: usegalaxy.org (v26.2.rc1) has **no** RNA secondary-structure folding tool. I exhausted the options:

| Attempt | Result |
|---|---|
| `search_tools_by_name`: RNAfold, vienna, RNAstructure, "secondary structure", fold, mfe, hairpin | 0 relevant hits (only `garnier`, which is *protein* SS) |
| `get_tool_panel` — all 79 sections, incl. "RNA Analysis (deprecated)" | no folding tool (Cufflinks/TopHat era only) |
| structurefold `predict_pipeline/1.0` ("RNA Structure Prediction", supports a ViennaRNA backend) | **broken on this server.** Job `bbd44e69cb8906b58184ad5d059856ad` exit 1: `predict_RNAs.py line 189: print filepath → SyntaxError: Missing parentheses in call to 'print'` — Python-2 wrapper on a Python-3 interpreter. Dies before reading input, so no input combination can fix it. |
| `create_user_tool` with a ViennaRNA biocontainer (my preferred route: `RNAfold -p --noPS`) | **403** `err_code 403005: "User is not allowed to run unprivileged tools"` — this account cannot create user-defined tools |

So I could not compute MFE values. I will not invent them.

## What I did establish

I read the file from Galaxy — it was not at the local path (`upload_file` returned "File not found" for the working directory and the scratchpad), but it is already on the server as **hid 20, `rna.fasta`**, dataset `f9cad7b01a4721358677534542e25d9f`, in history `bbd44e69cb8906b597074ed46423d4af` ("platform-benchmark fixtures"), SHA-256 `aa8e9ba0…3ff7e`, 141 bytes, 2 sequences.

```
>hairpin_test
GGGAAAUCCCGCGCUUCGGCGCGGGAUUUCCCAAAAAA                                      (38 nt)
>trna_like
GCGGAUUUAGCUCAGUUGGGAGAGCGCCAGACUGAAGAUCUGGAGGUCCUGUGUUCGAUCCACAGAAUUCGCACCA (76 nt)
```

**`hairpin_test` — base pairing worked out by hand from the sequence (exact, not predicted):**

```
GGGAAAUCCCGCGCUUCGGCGCGGGAUUUCCCAAAAAA
((((((((((((((....))))))))))))))......
```

Pairs (1,32) through (14,19) — **14 consecutive Watson–Crick pairs, zero mismatches, zero bulges, zero internal loops**: G1-C32, G2-C31, G3-C30, A4-U29, A5-U28, A6-U27, U7-A26, C8-G25, C9-G24, C10-G23, G11-C22, C12-G21, G13-C20, C14-G19 (10 G·C + 4 A·U). The loop is U15-U16-C17-G18 closed by C14-G19 — i.e. the canonical **5'-cUUCGg-3' tetraloop**, the most thermodynamically stable tetraloop known. Residues 33–38 (`AAAAAA`) are a free 3' tail.

**`trna_like`** is, from my own knowledge (not a database lookup I performed), the unmodified **yeast tRNA-Phe** sequence. Its native fold is the **cloverleaf: four separate helices** (acceptor stem 1–7/66–72, D-arm, anticodon arm, T-arm) joined at a four-way multibranch junction. It is structurally not a hairpin at all, and tRNA-Phe is a known case where MFE folding often fails to recover the cloverleaf without the natural base modifications.

So the qualitative verdict is unambiguous and does not depend on the missing numbers. The free energies themselves I cannot supply.

**To get them**, either works:
- `RNAfold -p --noPS < rna.fasta` locally (ViennaRNA) — gives MFE, ensemble free energy, centroid, and MFE frequency in the ensemble, which is the right "cleanliness" metric;
- or run the `rnateam` **RNAfold** tool on **usegalaxy.eu**, which has it installed — I'd need a `connect(url, api_key)` key for that instance.

Say the word and I'll run it the moment either is available. The empty history I created (`bbd44e69cb8906b5aa84f368e0af5b8b`) can be deleted; tell me if you want that.

## ANSWER

**Cleaner hairpin: `hairpin_test`, decisively.** It is a single uninterrupted stem-loop — 14 consecutive canonical base pairs (10 G·C, 4 A·U), no bulges or internal loops, capped by the maximally stable `cUUCGg` UUCG tetraloop, plus a 6-nt unpaired 3' poly-A tail: `((((((((((((((....))))))))))))))......`

`trna_like` (unmodified yeast tRNA-Phe, 76 nt) is **not a hairpin** — it folds as a four-helix cloverleaf around a multibranch junction, so "hairpin cleanliness" does not apply to it.

**UNABLE: free energies.** No RNA folding tool exists on usegalaxy.org (verified across all 79 tool-panel sections); the one candidate wrapper, structurefold `predict_pipeline/1.0`, is broken by a Python-2 `print` SyntaxError (job `bbd44e69cb8906b58184ad5d059856ad`); and creating a user-defined tool with a ViennaRNA container is forbidden for this account (HTTP 403, `err_code 403005`). I have no other folding tool in this session, and I will not supply ΔG values I did not compute.
